name: LibraryApp sources
description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI: the window with its thumbnail grid, the loupe (one photo on CanvasViewport at its own pixel size, its render or a placeholder, with its position readout, arrow keys and Escape), the inspector (one InspectorHeader above its Info and Develop tabs, library.inspector.header: the catalog's inspectorHeader, the collection's name and photo count with nothing selected, one photo's name, Captured, Size and Kind, or several photos' count and capture span) and its metadata inspector for the selected photos (rating, flag, color label), and the File > Load Sample Photos, View > Grid and Loupe, View > Sort By and thumbnail size commands, and the loupe area (View > Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom to Fit and Actual Size, Home and End, renders through a latest-wins RenderQueue on the loupe service, and the neighbours prefetched), and the thumbnails area, whose LibraryThumbnailStore holds the grid's images apart from the catalog so a thumbnail pass reruns the grid and not the window's body, and the crop area (Photo > Crop, R and Return, the loupe's crop frame overlay with its handles, drags and arrow nudges, and the Develop tab's CROP section: aspect chips, Straighten, Auto, Apply, Cancel and Reset Crop), and the status row under the grid and the loupe (LibraryStatusBar: the catalog's statusRow through ViewerStatusBar, its count or pixel size, selection, cell size, Fit and place, import, render, save and Preview data pills, each library.status.<id> with its help; no row on an empty live catalog), and the filters area (LibraryFilterBar: the Picked, Unflagged and Rejected chips, the rating and label menus, Hide Rejected, the filter summary and Clear; LibraryFiltersMenu, the filter and collection actions the focused window publishes as libraryFilters; and the collections.json hooks through CollectionsStore), and file-flow: the suite's Open Recent and Open In commands and app switching (SuiteFileCommands and suiteApp on LibraryShell's SuiteDocumentsBridge) and file drops on the whole window (suiteFileDrop into the catalog's perform), and XMPSidecarWriter, the file-system sidecar writer (only a .xmp path, never a photo file or another app's sidecar, written atomically).
